newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Argyle denies causing Indian diamond problems.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Argyle denies causing Indian diamond problems.

text.p: Argyle Diamonds, which manages the world's largest diamond mine, had not precipitated difficulties in the Indian diamond cutting industry, Argyle Diamonds managing director Gordon Gilchrist said.

Gilchrist said he denied suggestions by the Central Selling Organisation (CSO), operated by De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd, that Argyle Diamonds had created difficult conditions in the Indian diamond market.
"We believe that the current concerns in India are due to the very large volumes of rough diamonds sold by the CSO themselves," he said in a statement.

Argyle, which is 60 percent owned by the RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd group and 40 percent owned by Ashton Mining Ltd, split in June from the CSO cartel which controls the majority of the world's diamond market.
"In the second quarter this year, in the lead up to the expiry of the contract with Argyle, CSO sales into this market were at least 60 percent above normal levels," Gilchrist said.

"The recent decision by Argyle to sell its production direct to the market rather than through the CSO represents only a change in the distribution channel, not an increase in supply to the market from the Argyle mine," he said.
"Our priority is to work with our customers to help expand the world market for Argyle diamonds, in the interests of Argyle and the Indian diamond cutting industry," Gilchrist said.
